subject: ADR-184: a push script pushes once -- run again after its slice is in HEAD it pushes an undelivered commit or does nothing, never the next slice's changes under this slice's message
body: THE SECOND RUN. push-adr182.ps1 was run a second time after ADR-183 had landed on disk; it did what it was written to do -- git add its paths, which ADR-183 had just changed (the ledgers, the board, counts, AI_HARNESS, the lab task, verify_eco) -- and committed them under ADR-182's message, leaving ADR-183's own files (its manifest, its ADR, the _lab_charts module verify_eco imports) uncommitted: origin held a suite importing a module origin did not have. The script had no notion of having run. A manifest with "once": true now generates a guard before the chain and before any add: git ls-tree HEAD -- tools/delivery/<id>.json; if the slice's own manifest is in HEAD, push when rev-list --count @{u}..HEAD is above zero, else say already pushed -- nothing to do, the modified paths belong to a later slice, run its script -- and exit 0. Manifests without the key generate what they did, so every earlier script still passes --check. verify_delivery 36 -> 43 (the guard's text: what it asks, where it sits, what it does, that it stages nothing); mutate_delivery 30 -> 34/34. adr184.json is the first manifest with the key; its chain probe is tools/verify/_lab_charts.py, so push-adr184.ps1 runs push-adr183.ps1 first and lands ADR-183's five uncommitted files. No page was edited.
